speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Schools) what measures are being taken to foster an ethics-based education system in Singapore centred on values and character development and not just academic achievements.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In MOE, we agree and we are very passionate about the fact that imparting the right values and character development are central to our mission of education.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Besides nurturing such values, we also focus on developing social and emotional competencies of self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, relationship management and responsible decision-making.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: And this carefully designed curriculum then allows our students to learn through stories  because that is the best way for them to learn and internalise and through discussions, as well as engage in activities, learning journeys and reflections.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: The Member would agree that values are not just taught.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: And that is why MOE creates many opportunities for our students to apply what they have learnt to put into practice the values they have learnt.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In our schools, the "Values in Action" projects, class and leadership responsibility, Physical Education (PE) lessons, for example, inter-class games, project work and also Co-Curricular Activities (CCAs) are all part of the moulding process where it gives a lot of opportunities for our young to apply what they have learnt about character development and with a view of shaping our young into men and women of good character.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Along the way, our students receive feedback about their development from their teachers and their peers, and this is summed up by the form teacher in the Holistic Development Profiles at the end of each school year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: To shape our young generation, we also need role models of exemplary character.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In the selection of our teachers and school leaders, MOE looks for people with integrity, essentially role models who embrace and exemplify the core values that I have talked about earlier.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In training, NIE makes it a point to focus on Character and Citizenship development.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: It also equips teachers with the skills and knowledge to impart love for Singapore and our core values.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Other than that, workshops and seminars are also held every year for in-service teachers and key personnel to allow them to refresh and deepen their capabilities in values education.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In recent years, our schools and MOE have increased efforts to share all these development and efforts, and to involve our parents, very important stakeholders in values education.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In fact, our Primary school textbooks and Parent Support Groups (PSG) offer opportunities for family time, with suggested fun activities for family bonding and through the process, also value development.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
text: This consistently weaves a set of important values around our students, not just in school but at home, in school and also society, through Values In Action projects, and that really helps to set a sound foundation for their character growth.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: On the issue of character and CCA, if a child wants to participate in school in a team sport, just to be able to learn team spirit, camaraderie, values on the field and selflessness, would the school allow that child to participate notwithstanding that the child is not of a school team standard?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Why I asked is, parents and some residents have shared with me that some schools are too "medals-focused" when it comes to sports.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, this prevents students, who are just wanting to participate for the sake of participating and understanding what sport can provide to them, from doing so.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, would team sports be a vehicle of character building in schools?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member for the supplementary question and I want to reassure him and the other Members that we agree that whether it is PE or CCA team sports or even uniformed groups, these are very good platforms for our students, our young ones to understand the importance of teamwork, perseverance, resilience and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And this is really in line with our focus for "Values In Action", which was reframed from the Community Involvement Projects (CIP).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Whether it is the PE lessons or lessons in class, or the way we look at sports participation, we are looking at how we can avail such opportunities on a broad-base basis to our students to allow them to develop the six important values that I have talked about.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The reason I ask this is that many of my residents, they recall very favourably the 好公民 lessons during their times.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They are asking whether this is still taught in schools.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask whether are there such checks and whether 好公民 is still taught in school?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure the Member, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, there is a framework for guiding how the curriculum is implemented in the classroom.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is not what just you learn from the textbooks, it is also about applying it in the school environment, whether it is cleaning and respecting teachers and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The other 40 hours of school-designed CCE includes assembly programmes and also leadership development programmes.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I am a mother of two young boys, 8 and 11 years old, and so I check their bags every night and I see their textbooks.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They do have an activity book that they have to do; not just copy and do 习字 but also do a simple activity with the parents.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, I can attest to that, as a parent myself.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The 60 hours at the Secondary level comprise CCE lessons, school-based CCE would be similar to the pre-University assembly programmes and guidance modules.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This includes education, career guidance, cyber-wellness – very important for young ones now – and sexuality education.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, the curriculum time is not just set broadly; it is guided through a carefully designed curriculum to be taught, not just in the classroom, but also within the school environment.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: If values and character-based development are so important in one's education, can MOE then take these into account in crucial milestone decisions, such as entry into schools of choice of the students, or especially for the high-stake examinations, or in decisions such as the awarding of scholarships, and also entry into Institutions of Higher Learning (IHLs)?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Is there any way by which MOE can strengthen the alignment between the importance of this aspect of education with all the other crucial decisions in our education system?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member, Ms Denise Phua, for her very thoughtful suggestions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want to assure her that MOE is generally moving in that direction.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member would have taken note of Acting Minister Ong Ye Kung's sharing that for higher education, the institutes are also given some discretion to assess and enrol students, not just looking at their academic results, but looking at their holistic development and their character development.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For the second point, maybe, it is useful for me to take the opportunity to share that we do work with our schools to use the School Excellence model to evaluate their efforts and programmes about character development and citizenship through a few ways: students' feedback, survey and school-based indication.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: One example is schools have been giving out school awards for good character.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Some of these awards are familiar to many Members in this House.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They range from individual awards at the class level, at the school level with badges or certificates given, and even group awards, such as the "Most Responsible Class".

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If you talk to the IHL principals and faculty members, over the last four years, they do take note of students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Everything being equal, they will look at the students who have been given those kind of awards, like the ECHA, because it would mean that this is a socially responsible Singaporean who would be able to contribute to the school and the society in the future.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the annual performance for teachers, one of the Key Result Areas is character development of students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: When we look at working with our teachers, we also work with them to ensure that this is an area they look at – working with their students to develop their character and imparting the right values.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We agree with the Member that this is important.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We need to take a holistic and systematic approach to ensure that there is consistency within the education system from the schools to IHLs.
